title: Rabbi Chanina ben Gamla
author: Aharon Hyman

paragraphs: He is mentioned in [Sanhedrin 111a](https://www.sefaria.org/Sanhedrin.111a.11-12), expounding the verse “[And Moses hastened and bowed](https://www.sefaria.org/Exodus.34.8),” etc.: “What did he see? Rabbi Chanina ben Gamla said: He saw ‘long-suffering.’” Some read there ben Gamliel. Hyman cites Tosefta Parah 4:8 for the following: “Rabbi Shimon said: I found Chanina ben Gamliel in Sidon”; the Gra reads Chanina ben Gamla. Hyman endorses this because Rabbi Shimon would not call Rabbi Chanina ben Gamliel “Chanina,” since Rabbi Chanina ben Gamliel was older than Rabbi Shimon. Hyman suggests that possibly his father’s name was Gamliel, and they called him Gamla to distinguish him from Rabbi Chanina ben Gamliel the Patriarch.

notes.text: Hyman endorses the Gra’s Gamla reading and argues that Rabbi Shimon would not have called the older Chanina ben Gamliel simply “Chanina.” The common father-name and distinguishing nickname are his suggestions.

The linked Bavli reads Chanina ben Gamla. The [consulted Tosefta](https://www.sefaria.org/Tosefta_Parah.4.5) has the meeting at 4:5, names Chanina ben Gamliel, and gives no location in the passage. Its [4:8](https://www.sefaria.org/Tosefta_Parah.4.8) concerns vessels. “In Sidon,” the reference 4:8, and the Gra’s reading are as Hyman reports them.
